Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Seattle WA
824 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

.SYNOPSIS...A frontal system will move out of Western Washington
into this evening. High pressure builds aloft over the Pacific 
Northwest Thursday and Friday, with just a slight chance of 
precipitation. The upper ridge further builds over the weekend 
for drier, warmer conditions. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH THURSDAY NIGHT/...Latest radar
imagery shows rain showers dissipating over the region, along
with the convergence zone in Snohomish County. Impressive QPF 
amounts the last 24 hours over the western slopes of the 
Olympics and North Cascades, with 2-3.5 inches of rainfall over 
these areas. The previous discussion can be found below along 
with updates to the aviation and marine sections:

Drier conditions develop Wednesday into Thursday as high 
pressure begins to build into the Pacific Northwest. Morning 
stratus and localized areas of fog due to residual moisture will
clear for some sunshine during the afternoon. A system will
weaken along the northern periphery of the ridge late Thursday,
resulting in a slight uptick in rainfall potential beginning
later Thursday into Thursday night, however any QPF amounts are
expected to remain light, mainly focused on areas near the BC
border. Highs mainly in the low to mid 60s Wednesday and
Thursday.

&&

.LONG TERM /FRIDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...The aforementioned 
weakening system may continue to bring light rain along the 
northern tier, mainly North Cascades on Friday, but 
predominantly dry conditions are expected. Ensembles are in good
agreement in the upper ridge building further over the Western 
US this weekend, with dry conditions and warming temperatures 
over Western Washington. Dry conditions look to continue into 
early next week, although an increase in onshore flow may result
in slightly cooler temperatures by Monday. JD

&&

.AVIATION...
Westerly flow aloft will continue into Wednesday with an upper ridge 
axis centered well south of the region. Post-frontal low level 
onshore flow will weaken overnight and become northerly on 
Wednesday. Weak convergence persists over central Puget Sound this 
evening producing a few showers and MVFR ceilings. Confidence in the 
overall forecast ceilings areawide overnight is not high. However, 
lighter surface winds and remnant low level moisture will favor the 
development of IFR or low MVFR stratus. Stratus that does form will 
lift and scatter toward midday on Wednesday with varying amounts of 
mid and high level moisture streaming across the area. 

KSEA...As referenced above, MVFR ceilings are likely to hang around 
overnight and may drop to occasional IFR toward daybreak before 
lifting and scattering out toward 19Z or 20Z on Wednesday. Surface 
winds N/NE 6 to 9 knots easing overnight then becoming N/NW 7 to 10 
knots Wednesday afternoon. 

27

&&

.MARINE...
Surface high pressure building over the interior of British Columbia 
and weak troughing just offshore will lead to the development of 
some weak east/southeast flow on Thursday. Northerly or weak 
offshore flow will develop across area waters later Friday into the 
weekend as a thermally induced surface trough expands northward 
along the coast. 

27
